scope: Explicit Node or Java/Maven + Python unittest adapters; configuration is bound to original workflow and Host evidence.
adaptations: Explicit versioned lean_execution policy replaces the legacy argv recognition policy; no runtime source rewriting.
Policy checks adapter command shape and write ownership; actual runner statistics and stable test/subject hashes decide test success.
Protect Definition.json, Solution.json, Code.json and Delivery.json in addition to retained legacy artifact names.
Node syntax compilation enumerates all tracked production JS modules (bounded to 8), executes node --check on each, and reports per-file results; original non-Node compile policies remain unchanged.
Reject unsupported or unknown production source extensions, including declared expectedFiles, instead of treating Node entry-point syntax as their compilation.

Retained repair rules accept an explicit command-validator callback (legacy default unchanged); lean policy binds the original failed adapter argv, files, subjects, timeout, fingerprints and nonzero real test counts before all original task/spec/AC/evidence checks.

Java adapter admits root-project Maven compile with only quiet/offline/batch/no-transfer-progress flags; rejects skip, alternate pom and partial module options. Every successful Python batch/rerun/E2E binds its latest same-workspace/task compilation source list and SHA.

Remove duplicate business verdicts; retain only command/ownership/performance and original failed-test repair policies. Extract unchanged safe_path into safe_paths.py. Workflow identity is injected by the compiler.
workflowIdentity: Compiler bindResourceDigests.workflowSha256 over declared resource bytes
